subject: Clarify BlueHarbor connector operational carveouts & SOW boundary
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@blueharbor.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@blueharbor.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BlueHarbor - initial DPA redlines + operational carveouts

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the connector looks promising and the engineering team is keen to pilot. Attached are our DPA redlines (see key pages 3-5) and a short procurement note that summarizes three operational carveouts we need to see:

- Data residency assurance for EU-only datasets (we host in Frankfurt)
- Subprocessor notification window to be 30 days, not 14
- Audit log retention and exportability (we need logs retained 2 years in an immutable format)

We added inline comments where we think the SOW should capture the pilot scope and the acceptance criteria (attachment: BlueHarbor_DPA_redlines.pdf). Procurement is copied with a short list of billing/credit questions.

Can Laura confirm if Redwood can accept a 30-day subprocessor notice and whether the SOW can include a pilot-specific retention exception? If not, what mitigations do you propose?

Best,
Elena Morales
Sr. Partnerships Manager
BlueHarbor Analytics

[attachment: BlueHarbor_DPA_redlines.pdf (pdf)]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@blueharbor.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor - initial DPA redlines + operational carveouts

Elena — thanks for sending these over and for the candid list. I think we can solve all three items but want to confirm the intended permanent state vs pilot exceptions.

Quick plan:
1) Laura (legal) will review the DPA redlines and call out any non-starters or language we can accept with equivalent controls.
2) Ben (sales) and I will scope the SOW amendment to include a pilot carveout for residency and retention, with explicit acceptance criteria and a sunset if you move to production.
3) Can we do a 30-minute call tomorrow 10:30am PT to align on the retention/exportability format (CSV vs S3 immutability) and procurement asks? If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short mutual action plan.

Cc’ing Ben to confirm availability and to thread in pricing/credits.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference

[attachment: Proposed_SOW_amendment_v2.docx (docx) — draft outline]

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@blueharbor.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor - initial DPA redlines + operational carveouts

Hi Elena,

Appreciate the detail. High-level responses below — I’ll follow with annotated redline excerpts by EOD tomorrow.

- Subprocessor notice: We typically offer 30 days for significant new subprocessors, but for routine infrastructure changes we keep to 14. For a contract, we can accept 30 days if BlueHarbor requires it for compliance; we would ask for a reciprocal SLA for notices and a rollback plan for critical outages.

- Data residency: For our hosted Connector we can enforce region pinning for the pilot if the dataset is tagged and access-controlled; for production we recommend a VPC-private deployment (Redwood Private) and will put that into the SOW as an upsell/option with timeline.

- Audit logs: We can provide exportable immutable logs to S3 with lifecycle controls. Need to confirm retention length and format (audit trail vs full request/response payloads). Two years retention is substantial — we can do it but price and storage responsibilities must be explicit in the SOW.

Items we need from BlueHarbor to finalize language:
1) A short note on the specific datasets you want region-locked.
2) Whether the two-year retention is for metadata only or full payloads.
3) Procurement’s preferred billing cadence and whether you expect credits during the pilot window.

I’ll attach the legal excerpt and an initial SOW paragraph suggesting a 90-day pilot carveout window with a defined handoff to Private deployment if production residency is required.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

[attachment: Redwood_DPA_response_excerpt.pdf (pdf)]

From: Elena Morales <elena@blueharbor.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@blueharbor.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor - initial DPA redlines + operational carveouts

Laura — thanks for the quick read. Answers inline below and attaching a short procurement memo.

- Datasets: We’ll tag two datasets for the pilot (BH-EU-Events, BH-EU-Meta). We need those to remain in EU region for both storage and inference.

- Retention: We only need full payload retention for BH-EU-Events (search/audit purposes); metadata-only for BH-EU-Meta.

- Pilot credits: Procurement is requesting a 25% consumption credit for the first 90 days of the pilot while we validate integration and telemetry. They’ve attached an internal terms note (Procurement_Terms_Rowland.pdf).

We’re happy to do the 10:30am PT call tomorrow. Can you share proposed SOW language ahead of the call so our procurement/legal can review?

Best,
Elena

[attachment: Procurement_Terms_Rowland.pdf (pdf)]

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>

- Mutual action plan: 30-minute alignment call scheduled 2027-05-19 10:30am PT (calendar invite sent).

I am dropping a DocuSign link for the SOW amendment once Laura posts the redlines; if procurement agrees to the 20% pilot credit we can roll the SOW amendment and DPA redlines together for signature.
